claim: The CloudWatch agent is a software component that collects metrics, logs and traces from Amazon EC2 instances, on-premises servers and containerized applications, and it gives more comprehensive monitoring than the basic monitoring provided by default.
q: What does the CloudWatch agent collect and where can it run?
v: Amazon EC2 instances, on-premises servers, and containerized applications
more comprehensively than the basic monitoring
ev: The CloudWatch agent is a software component that collects metrics, logs, and traces from your Amazon EC2 instances, on-premises servers, and containerized applications. It enables you to monitor your infrastructure and applications more comprehensively than the basic monitoring provided by default.

claim: The CloudWatch agent collects internal system-level (in-guest) metrics from Amazon EC2 instances across operating systems, in addition to the metrics for the EC2 instances.
q: Which EC2 metrics does the CloudWatch agent add?
sc: per EC2 instance with the agent
ev: Collect internal system-level metrics from Amazon EC2 instances across operating systems. The metrics can include in-guest metrics, in addition to the metrics for Amazon EC2 instances.

claim: The CloudWatch agent collects system-level metrics from on-premises servers, including servers in a hybrid environment and servers not managed by AWS, and collects logs from Amazon EC2 instances and on-premises servers running Linux or Windows Server.
q: Can the CloudWatch agent monitor servers outside AWS?
v: running either Linux or Windows Server
ev: Collect system-level metrics from on-premises servers. These can include servers in a hybrid environment as well as servers not managed by AWS.
Collect logs from Amazon EC2 instances and on-premises servers, running either Linux or Windows Server.

claim: When the CloudWatch agent is installed on an Amazon EC2 instance, the metrics it collects are in addition to the metrics enabled by default on EC2 instances; it can also be installed on on-premises servers running Linux, Windows Server or macOS.
q: Does installing the CloudWatch agent replace the default EC2 metrics?
v: in addition to the metrics enabled by default
ev: You can collect metrics from servers by installing the CloudWatch agent on the server. You can install the agent on both Amazon EC2 instances and on-premises servers. You can also install the agent on computers running Linux, Windows Server, or macOS. If you install the agent on an Amazon EC2 instance, the metrics the agent collects are in addition to the metrics enabled by default on Amazon EC2 instances.

claim: The CloudWatch agent can collect memory metrics such as mem_used_percent (percentage of memory currently in use) and disk space metrics such as disk_used_percent (percentage of total disk space that is used) on Linux and macOS servers.
q: Which agent metrics report memory use and disk space use?
sc: Linux and macOS servers with the agent
n: No saved page states in one sentence that EC2 does not send memory or disk-space metrics by itself; only what the agent collects is claimed here.
ev:
| `mem_used_percent` | The percentage of memory currently in use.
Unit: Percent |

| `disk_used_percent` | The percentage of total disk space that is used.
Unit: Percent |

claim: The default CloudWatch namespace for metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent is CWAgent, although you can specify a different namespace when you configure the agent.
q: Which namespace do CloudWatch agent metrics use by default?
ev: The default CloudWatch namespace for these metrics is `CWAgent`, although you can specify a different namespace when you configure the agent.

claim: Metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent are billed as custom metrics.
q: Are metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent free like default EC2 metrics?
v: Metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent
ev: Metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent are billed as custom metrics.

claim: The CloudWatch agent can send metrics to CloudWatch, to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, or to both, using the metrics_destinations parameter in the metrics section of its configuration file.
q: Can the CloudWatch agent send metrics to Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus?
v: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, or to both
ev: Send the metrics to either CloudWatch or Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, or to both. The CloudWatch agent configuration file contains a `metrics_destinations` parameter in the `metrics` section.

claim: Using the CloudWatch agent to collect traces removes the need to run a separate trace collection daemon, which reduces the number of agents you run and manage.
q: Can the CloudWatch agent replace the X-Ray daemon for collecting traces?
ev: Using the CloudWatch agent allows you to collect traces without needing to run a separate trace collection daemon, helping to reduce the number of agents that you run and manage.

claim: You can install the CloudWatch agent manually using the command line or integrate it with AWS Systems Manager; Systems Manager makes it easier to install the agent on a fleet of EC2 instances.
q: How can you install the CloudWatch agent on many instances?
v: integrate it with AWS Systems Manager
a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances
ev: You can download and install the CloudWatch agent manually using the command line, or you can integrate it with AWS Systems Manager.
Using AWS Systems Manager makes it easier to install the CloudWatch agent on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances.

claim: When you install the CloudWatch agent through Systems Manager, the IAM role attached to the instance must have the CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy attached.
q: Which IAM policy must the instance role have for the CloudWatch agent?
v: IAM role attached to the instance
ev: You must also make sure that the IAM role attached to the instance has the **CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy** attached.

claim: You can save the CloudWatch agent configuration file in the Systems Manager Parameter Store and reuse it when you install the agent on other servers.
q: Where can you store a shared CloudWatch agent configuration?
v: install the agent on other servers
ev: After you have a CloudWatch agent configuration saved in Parameter Store, you can use it when you install the agent on other servers.

claim: The unified CloudWatch agent is the newer agent for CloudWatch Logs; if you use the older CloudWatch Logs agent, AWS recommends migrating with the wizard in the new agent package, which reads your current configuration and sets up the new agent to collect the same logs.
q: What does AWS recommend when you still use the older CloudWatch Logs agent?
v: migrate to using the new unified agent
the wizard included in the new agent package
ev: If you are currently using the older CloudWatch Logs agent and want to migrate to using the new unified agent, we recommend that you use the wizard included in the new agent package.
This wizard can read your current CloudWatch Logs agent configuration file and set up the CloudWatch agent to collect the same logs.

claim: The CloudWatch embedded metric format lets you generate custom metrics asynchronously as logs written to CloudWatch Logs; CloudWatch automatically extracts the custom metrics so you can visualize and alarm on them.
q: How can an application produce custom metrics by writing logs?
v: CloudWatch automatically extracts the custom metrics
ev: The CloudWatch embedded metric format allows you to generate custom metrics asynchronously in the form of logs written to CloudWatch Logs. You can embed custom metrics alongside detailed log event data, and CloudWatch automatically extracts the custom metrics so that you can visualize and alarm on them, for real-time incident detection.

claim: The embedded metric format helps you create custom metrics from ephemeral resources such as Lambda functions and containers without instrumenting or maintaining separate code.
q: Why use the embedded metric format for Lambda functions and containers?
v: ephemeral resources such as Lambda functions and containers
without having to instrument or maintain separate code
ev: Embedded metric format helps you generate actionable custom metrics from ephemeral resources such as Lambda functions and containers. By using the embedded metric format to send logs from these ephemeral resources, you can now easily create custom metrics without having to instrument or maintain separate code, while gaining powerful analytical capabilities on your log data.

claim: To generate metrics from logs with the embedded metric format you need the logs:PutLogEvents permission; you do not also need the cloudwatch:PutMetricData permission.
q: Which IAM permission does the embedded metric format need?
ev: To generate metrics from logs with embedded metric format, you need the `logs:PutLogEvents` permission but you don't need to also have the `cloudwatch:PutMetricData` permission.

claim: If you unintentionally use high-cardinality dimensions such as requestId, the embedded metric format by design creates a custom metric for each unique dimension combination, which raises your custom metric usage and bill.
q: Why can the embedded metric format raise the CloudWatch bill?
v: impacts your custom metric usage and corresponding bill
ev: Be careful when configuring your metric extraction as it impacts your custom metric usage and corresponding bill. If you unintentionally create metrics based on high-cardinality dimensions (such as `requestId`), the embedded metric format will by design create a custom metric corresponding to each unique dimension combination.

claim: With the embedded metric format, charges are incurred for log ingestion and archival and for the custom metrics that are generated.
q: What do you pay for with the embedded metric format?
ev: Charges are incurred for logs ingestion and archival, and custom metrics that are generated.

claim: Metric filters define the terms and patterns to look for in log data as it is sent to CloudWatch Logs, and CloudWatch Logs uses them to turn log data into numerical CloudWatch metrics that you can graph or set an alarm on.
q: How do you turn log events into a CloudWatch metric?
v: turn log data into numerical CloudWatch metrics
ev: Metric filters define the terms and patterns to look for in log data as it is sent to CloudWatch Logs. CloudWatch Logs uses these metric filters to turn log data into numerical CloudWatch metrics that you can graph or set an alarm on.

claim: Metric filters do not retroactively filter data: they publish metric data points only for events that happen after the filter was created.
q: Does a new metric filter count log events that were ingested before it was created?
v: events that happen after the filter was created
ev: Filters do not retroactively filter data. Filters only publish the metric data points for events that happen after the filter was created.

claim: Metric filters are supported only for log groups in the Standard log class.
q: Can you create a metric filter on an Infrequent Access log group?
ev: Metric filters are supported only for log groups in the Standard log class.

claim: If you assign dimensions to a metric created by a metric filter, you cannot assign a default value for that metric.
q: Can a metric filter with dimensions also have a default value?
v: metric created by a metric filter
ev: If you assign dimensions to a metric created by a metric filter, you can't assign a default value for that metric.

claim: Metric math lets you query multiple CloudWatch metrics and use math expressions to create new time series from them, for example dividing the Lambda Errors metric by the Invocations metric to get an error rate.
q: How can you combine existing metrics into a new one without publishing a custom metric?
v: use math expressions to create new time series
divide the `Errors` metric by the `Invocations` metric
ev: Metric math enables you to query multiple CloudWatch metrics and use math expressions to create new time series based on these metrics. You can visualize the resulting time series on the CloudWatch console and add them to dashboards. Using AWS Lambda metrics as an example, you could divide the `Errors` metric by the `Invocations` metric to get an error rate.

claim: If you call PutMetricData with a new metric name, CloudWatch creates the metric for you; otherwise it associates the data with the existing metric you specified.
q: Do you have to create a custom metric before you publish data to it?
v: CloudWatch creates a metric for you
associates your data with the existing metric
ev: If you call this command with a new metric name, CloudWatch creates a metric for you. Otherwise, CloudWatch associates your data with the existing metric that you specified.

claim: For new implementations, the CloudWatch documentation recommends publishing custom metrics with OpenTelemetry instead of the PutMetricData API.
q: What does CloudWatch recommend for publishing custom metrics in new implementations?
ev: For new implementations, we recommend using OpenTelemetry to publish custom metrics.
